statement: The bar chart shows how many people visited a small museum on each day from Monday to Friday. On Saturday the number of visitors was 50% more than the mean number of visitors per weekday. How many people visited on Saturday?

figure.alt: A bar chart of museum visitors per day, on an axis labelled every 10 with gridlines every 5: Monday 40, Tuesday 25, Wednesday 35, Thursday 30, Friday 50.

choices.misconception: I found the mean for the five weekdays and forgot to add the extra 50 percent.
I added 50 percent to Friday, the busiest day, instead of to the mean.
I took 50 percent of the five-day total of 180 instead of working from the mean.
I added 50 percent to the five-day total of 180 instead of to the mean.

hints: Read all five bars carefully, including the two that end between labels.
First find the mean: total the five readings and share the total equally among the days. Then '50% more' means the mean plus half of the mean again.
The five bars total 180, so the mean is 36. Half of 36 is 18.

solutions.reliable: From the chart: 40 + 25 + 35 + 30 + 50 = 180 visitors, so the mean is 180 / 5 = 36 per weekday. Fifty percent more is 36 + 18 = 54. The transferable idea: read every value before calculating, and apply a percentage to exactly the quantity the sentence names.

whyOnTest: Reading a chart and then applying a percentage to the right base (the mean, not the total or the tallest bar) is a two-step data skill.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
